Full domain summary statistics of model performance¶

Taylor diagrams for the sea surface¶

Figure 1: Taylor diagram for sea surface annual mean of Total Alkalinity, KD490, Oxygen, Nitrate, Salinity, Silicate, Temperature (ZISSOUCLIMATOLOGY), pH, Temperature (ZISSOUSST), Chlorophyll, Phosphate. This diagram compares climatological annual averages of the model and observations across the model's spatial domain. Standard devaiation is normalized by the standard deviation of the observations, and a standard deviation below 1 indicates that the model is less variable than the observations. Note: This figure summarizes the overall ability of the model to reproduce climatological spatial patterns, and it does not represent temporal performance.

Temporal performance of the model at the sea surface¶

Figure 2: Spatial correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient) between model and observations for annual mean of total alkalinity, KD490, dissolved oxygen, nitrate concentration, salinity, silicate concentration, sea temperature, pH, sea temperature, chlorophyll concentration, phosphate concentration. This figure compares climatological monthly averages of the model and observations across the model's spatial domain.

The overall ability of the model reproduce the seasonality of each variable was estimated by calculating the spatial mean of the Pearson correlation coefficient between the model and the observations. The spatial mean was calculated by averaging the correlation coefficient of each grid cell.

Table 3: Spatial average of the temporal correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient) between model and observations for annual mean of nitrate concentration, phosphate concentration, sea temperature, salinity, KD490, sea temperature, chlorophyll concentration, silicate concentration, dissolved oxygen. The correlation is calculated for each grid cell individually using monthly climatological averages. The spatial average is then calculated for each variable.

Perfomance of model across depths¶

Root mean square deviation (RMSD), bias and correlation between model and observations were calculated for each variable at different depths. The RMSD is calculated as the square root of the mean of the squared differences between the model and observations. The bias is calculated as the modelled spatial mean minus the observational spatial mean. The correlation is calculated for each variable at different depths.
